2021 / China / Print

Accessibility standard for textbooks

China’s GB 40070-2021 standard establishes health requirements for learning materials. This standard refers to the use of accessible font sizes and line spacing in school learning materials and classroom environments to help prevent and control myopia among children and adolescents.

Released in 2021 and implemented the following year, this standard applies to items such as textbooks, workbooks, examination papers, preschool reading materials, classroom lighting, reading/writing desk lamps, and teaching multimedia products.

The standard addresses the design and production of textbooks, workbooks, examination papers, preschool reading materials, classroom lighting, desk lamps, and teaching multimedia products. By treating visual health as a shared responsibility across publishing, product design, lighting, education, and procurement, the policy shows how communication materials can be regulated not only for content, but also for their physical and sensory impact on young audiences.

Criteria

  • EIRT1 / EnvironmentEnvironmental Impact Reduction

    The project strategy includes at least one action to reduce environmental impact that is supported by a qualified life cycle study (LCS) or quantitative life cycle assessment (LCA).

  • EIRT5 / EnvironmentPaper

    The project reduces paper use through efficiencies.

  • EIRT6 / EnvironmentProduct Quantity

    Reproduction is limited to immediate needs, including the possibility that no physical copies were needed.

  • EIRT7 / EnvironmentDurability & Extended Life

    The product or system is physically durable and has a longer life than the industry average, where desirable. The product or system can be reused, recharged, repaired, and/or upgraded as an environmental benefit.

  • EE3 / EnvironmentConsumer Energy Efficiency

    The product or system used by the consumer is energy efficient or uses renewable energy.

  • S9 / SocietyPrinted Documents and Compliance

    Printed materials are designed using accessible typography, contrast, hierarchy, and readability principles to support users with visual, cognitive, or literacy-related accessibility needs.

Related projects

Front-of-Package Food Warning Labels

Across Latin America, food warning labels have become one of the clearest examples of communication design used as part of public health policies. In addition to the use of small nutrition tables, or technical nutrition data, these “Excess Sugar,” “Excess Sodium,” “Excess Calories,” or “Excess Saturated Fats” labels are prominently placed on the front of food and beverage packaging.
